seoTitle: How to Change Card Color in Jira Using JQL
metaDescription: Customize Jira board card colors by work type, priority, or JQL query so you can spot priorities and issue types at a glance.
intro: A board full of same-colored cards makes it harder to spot what needs attention first. This guide shows how to change Jira card colors based on work type, priority, or a JQL query so your board becomes easier to scan visually.

steps.heading: Open your board settings
steps.body: Go to your Jira board's settings and find the card color configuration option.

steps.heading: Choose a coloring strategy
steps.body: Decide whether you want cards colored by issue type, priority, or a custom JQL-based condition.

steps.heading: Set colors by work type or priority
steps.body: Assign specific colors to each issue type or priority level so they're visually distinguishable at a glance.

steps.heading: Use JQL for custom conditions
steps.body: For more advanced rules, write a JQL query that defines exactly which cards should get a particular color.

steps.heading: Review your board's new look
steps.body: Check your board to confirm the colors are applying correctly and adjust as needed for clarity.

faq.question: Can I combine priority and work type coloring?
faq.answer: Board card color settings typically let you choose one coloring strategy at a time, so you'll want to pick the one most useful for your team.

faq.question: Do I need JQL knowledge to set custom card colors?
faq.answer: Basic JQL knowledge helps for custom conditions, but Jira also offers simpler built-in options like coloring by priority or issue type without writing queries.

faq.question: Will card color changes affect other team members' views?
faq.answer: Board-level color settings usually apply to everyone viewing that board, keeping the visual system consistent across the team.

faq.question: Can I reset card colors back to default?
faq.answer: Yes, you can return to the board settings at any time and switch the coloring option back to default.
